microtheory.name: anthropology
microtheory.definition: Anthropology — holistic study of humanity. Cultural, biological/physical, archaeological, linguistic subfields. Cultural relativism, ethnography, kinship, ritual, exchange. Boas, Malinowski, Mauss, Levi-Strauss, Geertz, Sahlins, Strathern. Substrate analogue: the comparative + holistic study of human variation across societies + time.

concepts.name: culture_anthropological
concepts.definition: Tylor 1871: complex whole including knowledge, belief, art, morals, law, custom + any other capabilities acquired by member of society. Substrate analogue: substrate's transmitted Mt-content.

concepts.name: cultural_relativism
concepts.definition: Franz Boas. Cultures judged by own internal standards, not foreign ones. Distinct from moral relativism. Substrate analogue: substrate's frame-relativism (Axiom 0 echo).

concepts.name: ethnocentrism
concepts.definition: Judging other cultures by own. Opposite of relativism. Pervasive cognitive bias.

concepts.name: holism_anthropological
concepts.definition: Anthropology aims at whole picture: biology + ecology + history + culture together. No domain in isolation.

concepts.name: cultural_anthropology
concepts.definition: Study of contemporary human cultures + variation. Ethnographic method.

concepts.name: archaeology
concepts.definition: Past cultures through material remains. Excavation + analysis. Stratigraphy + dating + typology.

concepts.name: biological_anthropology
concepts.definition: Human evolution + variation + primatology. Skeletal + genetic + comparative.

concepts.name: linguistic_anthropology
concepts.definition: Language as cultural practice + cognitive tool. Sapir-Whorf, ethnopoetics, conversation analysis.

concepts.name: ethnography
concepts.definition: Long-term immersive fieldwork producing thick descriptive account of culture. Malinowski's Trobriand Islands template.

concepts.name: participant_observation
concepts.definition: Researcher participates in community life while observing. Tension: insider/outsider.

concepts.name: thick_description_geertz
concepts.definition: Clifford Geertz 1973. Interpretive ethnography giving rich context + meaning, not just behavior. Ryle's wink vs twitch.

concepts.name: emic_etic
concepts.definition: Pike. Emic = insider's perspective + categories. Etic = outsider's analytical framework. Both needed.

concepts.name: kinship_systems
concepts.definition: Anthropology's classical core. How societies organise family, descent, marriage. Patrilineal, matrilineal, bilateral, cognatic.

concepts.name: lineage
concepts.definition: Group of relatives descended from common ancestor through known links. Substrate analogue: substrate's genealogical chain.

concepts.name: exogamy_endogamy
concepts.definition: Marriage outside (exo) vs inside (endo) defined group. Levi-Strauss: incest taboo as universal.

concepts.name: gift_exchange_mauss
concepts.definition: Marcel Mauss 1925 'The Gift'. Obligation to give, receive, reciprocate. Foundation of pre-market economies + much current social bonding.

concepts.name: potlatch
concepts.definition: Northwest Coast ceremonial competitive gift-giving. Status from giving away. Counter-utilitarian. Substrate analogue: substrate's reputation-via-generosity.

concepts.name: kula_ring
concepts.definition: Trobriand inter-island ceremonial exchange documented by Malinowski. Necklaces clockwise, armshells counter. Establishes long-term alliances.

concepts.name: reciprocity_sahlins
concepts.definition: Marshall Sahlins. Generalised (no expectation) + balanced (immediate equivalent) + negative (taking) reciprocity along social-distance spectrum.

concepts.name: ritual
concepts.definition: Patterned symbolic action. Turner's liminality, Van Gennep's rites of passage (separation, liminal, reintegration). Substrate analogue: substrate's repeated structural enactment.

concepts.name: rite_of_passage
concepts.definition: Van Gennep 1909. Transition between social statuses. Three phases: separation, liminal, reintegration.

concepts.name: liminality
concepts.definition: Victor Turner. Threshold state between identities. Anti-structural communitas. Substrate analogue: substrate's transition between basin states.

concepts.name: taboo
concepts.definition: Polynesian tapu. Prohibited contact + speech. Douglas: dirt as matter out of place. Substrate analogue: substrate's category-violation rejection.

concepts.name: structural_anthropology
concepts.definition: Claude Lévi-Strauss. Cultures as systems of binary oppositions (raw/cooked, nature/culture). Universal cognitive structures.

concepts.name: functionalism_malinowski
concepts.definition: Bronisław Malinowski. Cultural institutions serve individual biological needs. Functional integration.

concepts.name: structural_functionalism_radcliffe_brown
concepts.definition: Radcliffe-Brown. Institutions function to maintain social structure (not individual need).

concepts.name: interpretive_anthropology
concepts.definition: Geertz. Culture as text to be read. Webs of meaning humans spin + are suspended in.

concepts.name: ontological_turn
concepts.definition: Viveiros de Castro + others. Different cultures may have different ontologies (worlds), not just different interpretations of one world.

concepts.name: human_universals_brown
concepts.definition: Donald Brown 1991. Features attested in every documented society — language, kinship, music, time concept, gossip, etc. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded foundational Mts.

rules.name: cultures_must_be_understood_internally
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates a cultural practice
rules.body: judge by internal categories + values, not external. Cultural relativism (Boas). Substrate's frame-relative evaluation.

rules.name: ethnography_requires_extended_immersion
rules.head: Jabberwock studies a culture
rules.body: deep understanding requires long-term participant observation — months to years. Short visits produce thin description.

rules.name: gift_creates_obligation
rules.head: Jabberwock observes gift exchange
rules.body: the gift carries the giver's identity; receiving creates obligation to reciprocate. Mauss 1925. Substrate's social-bond mechanism.

rules.name: rites_of_passage_structure_transition
rules.head: Jabberwock observes a social transition
rules.body: three phases: separation, liminal, reintegration. Van Gennep 1909. Substrate's transition pattern.

rules.name: thick_description_captures_meaning
rules.head: Jabberwock interprets a cultural practice
rules.body: thin description (behaviorist) misses meaning; thick description (Geertz) captures local interpretation. Substrate's context-rich interpretation.
